open_points.subject: Trial values for an inputless function
open_points.text: “a trial case's expected output the highest class of the case's inputs” and “a trial execution's output does” do not define the result when the contract has no input ports, although inputless functions are allowed
open_points.question: What disclosure class do expected outputs and trial-execution outputs receive for a trial case with no inputs?
options: open
Refuse expected outputs for an inputless contract
Another explicitly defined base class

open_points.subject: Execution class for an inputless function
open_points.text: “The class of an execution is the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs” has no result when an inputless function executes
open_points.question: What is the execution class, and therefore the class of its failure_detail, when an execution has no inputs?
options: open
Derive it from outputs when present
Leave such failure details undisclosed

open_points.subject: Disclosure through guarded control flow
open_points.text: Rule 2 assigns an operation output only the class declared for that output, while a guard may use another output of the same operation; the guard's class is not included in the guarded edge's reach class despite “No function, edge or flow construct lowers a class”
open_points.question: Does the disclosure class of a guard value taint the guarded delivery, its skip/production result, or the downstream values whose presence it controls?
options: Raise the guarded path to at least the guard port's class
Do not taint control flow and permit the guard outcome to be visible at the delivered value's class
Forbid guards whose class exceeds the guarded source value's class
open_points.default_guess: Raise the guarded path to at least the guard port's class

open_points.subject: Empty mapped operation output
open_points.text: At proof time an operation output has “the class its binding declares,” but at run time “A mapped operation over an empty list executes nothing, so its empty output lists take their class by A13 rule 6,” which is the highest class among the node's inputs
open_points.question: How must proof compute the possible class of a mapped operation output so an empty mapped input cannot produce a class above the downstream input's accepted class?
options: Use the maximum of the binding output class and all classes that can reach the mapped node's inputs
Always use the binding output class, including for an empty output list
Refuse delivery at run time if the empty list's derived class exceeds the target acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Use the maximum of the binding output class and all classes that can reach the mapped node's inputs

open_points.subject: Agent-visible failure-detail length
open_points.text: “A failure_detail whose class is above open ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class” does not define what the length measures
open_points.question: Is the disclosed failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 bytes after bounded truncation
Unicode scalar values after bounded truncation
Original untruncated byte length

open_points.subject: Service response containing an encoded credential
open_points.text: State 0 says credentials “never enter ... an answer,” while A17 says a service response carrying a credential in another encoding “is not recognised, and is protected only by its class” and A09 says it is kept like any other response
open_points.question: Must the kernel prevent encoded forms of a credential from reaching an answer, or is only a verbatim credential occurrence forbidden?
options: Only verbatim occurrences are detected and forbidden
No representation of a credential may reach an answer
Non-verbatim occurrences may be returned only to the owner
open_points.default_guess: Only verbatim occurrences are detected and forbidden

open_points.subject: Security checks during token-list configuration rereads
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file to be a regular, non-symbolic-link, owner-only file opened component by component, but A16 says “Exactly four checks apply to a re-read” and lists only parsing and token-list checks
open_points.question: When the configuration is reread for token changes, must the kernel repeat A17's ownership, mode, regular-file, and no-symlink checks, and what happens when one fails?
options: Repeat all A17 file-security checks and refuse every request on failure
Apply only A16's four checks after startup
Stop the kernel if an A17 file-security property changed
open_points.default_guess: Repeat all A17 file-security checks and refuse every request on failure

open_points.subject: Credential file text normalization and validation
open_points.text: The credential is “decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline” and is refused if it “holds ... a control character,” but neither “newline” nor “control character” is defined
open_points.question: Which trailing byte sequence is removed, whether exactly one or all such sequences are removed, and which Unicode or ASCII characters count as control characters?
options: Remove exactly one LF and reject ASCII controls including any remaining CR or LF
Remove exactly one LF or CRLF and reject ASCII CTLs plus DEL
Remove all trailing line endings and reject every Unicode control-category character
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one LF or CRLF and reject ASCII CTLs plus DEL

open_points.subject: Credential value placed in an HTTP header
open_points.text: A credential value may be any nonempty UTF-8 text without a control character and is “added as that header,” but the wire encoding and treatment of non-ASCII or leading/trailing whitespace are not stated
open_points.question: Which credential values are valid HTTP field values, and how are accepted non-ASCII characters and surrounding whitespace represented on the wire?
options: Restrict credentials to a defined ASCII field-value subset and preserve accepted bytes exactly
Encode accepted Unicode as UTF-8 bytes and preserve whitespace
Use the HTTP client's native header encoding and normalization
open_points.default_guess: Restrict credentials to a defined ASCII field-value subset and preserve accepted bytes exactly

open_points.subject: Installation startup validation
open_points.text: A17, A09, A03 and A18 each impose startup refusals, but no order is given among configuration-file security, credential-header collision, sandbox, data-directory and other startup checks
open_points.question: When several startup conditions fail, which check is performed and reported first?
options: Define one global startup-check order
Report all startup failures together in a defined order
Allow any failing startup check to be reported

open_points.subject: Ordering of propagation records versus executable nodes
open_points.text: The next executable node is the ready node with the smallest node_id, and nodes made impossible become skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed, but the rules do not say whether those derived records are written before or after another ready independent node executes
open_points.question: After a conclusion simultaneously makes some nodes non-executable and other nodes ready, must the kernel exhaust skip/upstream-failure propagation before selecting the next ready node, or execute ready nodes first?
options: Eagerly write all newly derivable skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed records, in the stated order, before executing another node
Execute the smallest ready node first and propagate non-executable nodes only when no ready node remains
Choose globally by node_id across executable and derived conclusions
open_points.default_guess: Eagerly write all newly derivable skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed records before executing another node

open_points.subject: Mapped-output size failure across kernel releases
open_points.text: A mapped value list over stored_value_bytes_max fails the node, but “No record of the node states that failure” and every reader derives it from the elements and stored_value_bytes_max; A20 permits a later release to change ceilings
open_points.question: Which stored fact fixes the ceiling used to derive this failure after restart or upgrade, so the run and trace cannot be reinterpreted differently by a later release?
options: Persist the applicable release or ceiling with the run
Persist an immutable aggregate-failure record
Always use the current release ceiling, allowing the derivation to change
open_points.default_guess: Persist the applicable release or ceiling with the run
